title: Short Encoding of Words
statement: An encoding of `words` is a reference string `s` that ends with `'#'` together with one start index per word, such that reading `s` from the start index of `words[i]` up to (not including) the first `'#'` after it gives exactly `words[i]`. Several words may share a start index or overlap inside `s`. Return the smallest possible length of `s` over all such encodings.
constraints: words[i] contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

A word can reuse another word's slot exactly when it is a **suffix** of that word: `"me"` starts inside `"time#"` and stops at the same `'#'`. So the shortest string writes each word that is not a suffix of another word once, followed by `'#'`, and every other word points into one of those. Checking every pair of words for the suffix relation works but costs O(n² · L). Reversing the words turns suffixes into prefixes, and a trie groups shared prefixes: a reversed word that is a suffix of another ends on a node that still has children.

## Approach

1. Build a trie of the distinct words, each inserted from its last letter to its first; every node is a `Map` from letter to child.
2. Remember in `ends` the node where each distinct word finishes.
3. A word whose end node has no children is not a suffix of any other word, so it needs its own `word.length + 1` characters.
4. Sum those lengths into `length` and return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`words = ["time", "me", "bell"]` are inserted as `"emit"`, `"em"` and `"lleb"`. `"em"` walks the existing path `e → m`, so its end node has the child `i`. The end nodes of `"time"` (`t`) and `"bell"` (`b`) have no children. The total is `(4 + 1) + (4 + 1) = 10`, the length of `"time#bell#"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · L) with `L ≤ 7`: every letter of every word is visited once.
- Space: O(n · L) for the trie nodes.

## Pitfalls

- Duplicates must be counted once; inserting `"a"` twice and counting both would double its cost.
- Only suffixes can share a slot; a prefix such as `"ab"` of `"abc"` still needs its own `"ab#"`.
- Each kept word costs one extra character for its `'#'`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `root` | the trie's root node (a `Map` from letter to child node) |
| `ends` | each distinct word mapped to the node where its reversed insertion stops |
| `node` | the current trie node while inserting or checking |
| `i` | index of the letter being inserted, moving from the end of the word |
| `length` | the encoding length built so far |
